name: data-table
description: Create a sortable, filterable data table component

promptLevels.novice: table that sorts when you click headers
promptLevels.beginner: make a data table class that can sort and filter rows
promptLevels.intermediate: create a DataTable class that stores an array of data, can sort by any column, and can filter rows based on a search term
promptLevels.advanced: write a generic DataTable class that takes an array of objects, allows sorting by clicking column names (ascending/descending), and can filter the data to show only rows matching a search string
promptLevels.expert: Write a DataTable class that manages tabular data with sorting and filtering capabilities. The class should: 1) Accept an array of data objects (generic type) where each object represents a row. 2) Store the original data and maintain a separate filtered/sorted view. 3) Provide a sort(column, direction) method that sorts the data by the specified column in 'asc' or 'desc' order. Sorting should work with strings (case-insensitive), numbers, and dates. 4) Provide a filter(searchTerm) method that filters rows to only include those where any column value contains the search term (case-insensitive). 5) Provide a getData() method that returns the currently filtered and sorted data. 6) Handle edge cases like sorting null/undefined values and filtering on various data types. The class should be generic and work with any object structure. {languageSpecific}

languageInstructions.typescript: Use TypeScript with generics: `class DataTable<T extends Record<string, any>>`. Define types for sort direction ('asc' | 'desc'), column keys (keyof T), and method parameters. The class should properly type the internal data arrays and sort/filter logic. Export the class.
languageInstructions.javascript: Create a DataTable class with constructor accepting initial data array. Use array methods like sort(), filter(), and includes() for implementation. Store both original data and current view. Handle type coercion for sorting different data types. Export the class as default.
languageInstructions.javascript-jsdoc: Use JSDoc with @template T for the generic data type, @typedef for SortDirection ('asc'|'desc'), @class for DataTable, @param with type information for all methods, and @returns with detailed return type descriptions. Document the sorting algorithm and filtering behavior. Export the class.

variants.typescript: Write a TypeScript DataTable generic class that can display, sort, and filter data. Include proper interfaces and generic types.
variants.javascript: Write a JavaScript DataTable class that can display, sort, and filter data.
variants.javascript-jsdoc: Write a JavaScript DataTable class with JSDoc that can display, sort, and filter data. Include generic type annotations.
variants.javascript-vanilla-web:
Create a data table component with sorting and filtering in vanilla JavaScript. Include:

**Features:**
- Display data in a table
- Column headers with sort indicators (↑↓)
- Click header to sort (ascending/descending/no sort)
- Search/filter input (filters all columns)
- Pagination (rows per page: 10, 25, 50)
- Row selection (checkbox)
- Responsive design

**HTML Structure:**
- Search input
- Table with thead and tbody
- Pagination controls
- Rows per page selector

**CSS:**
- Clean table design
- Striped rows
- Hover effects
- Sort indicators
- Mobile responsive (horizontal scroll on small screens)

**JavaScript:**
- DataTable class
- Methods: setData(), sort(), filter(), paginate()
- Event handlers for interactions
- Efficient re-rendering

**Sample Data:** Use user data (id, name, email, role, status)

Return as single HTML file with demo data.
variants.javascript-vanilla-web-jsdoc:
Same as javascript-vanilla-web, plus complete JSDoc:

- @typedef for Column definition
- @typedef for TableConfig
- @typedef for DataRow (generic)
- Document all methods
- Include usage examples in JSDoc

Return as single HTML file.
variants.typescript-vanilla-web:
Create a data table using TypeScript and vanilla Web APIs. Include:

**TypeScript:**
- Generic DataTable<T> class
- Interface for Column<T> (key, header, sortable, formatter)
- Interface for TableConfig
- Type-safe sorting and filtering
- Proper event typing

**Features:**
- Generic data type support
- Column configuration (sortable, formatter function)
- Multi-column sorting
- Global and per-column filtering
- Pagination
- Row selection
- Custom cell rendering

**Code Structure:**
- Separate TypeScript modules
- Clean separation of concerns
- No frameworks

Provide TypeScript source, HTML structure, and usage example.
variants.typescript-react:
Create a data table component using TypeScript React. Include:

**Components:**
- DataTable<T> (generic component)
- TableHeader
- TableBody
- TableRow
- TablePagination
- TableFilters

**TypeScript:**
- Generic component: DataTable<T>
- Column<T> interface (key, header, sortable, render?)
- TableProps<T> interface
- Type-safe sorting and filtering

**Features:**
- Generic data type support
- Sortable columns (multi-sort with shift-click)
- Global search
- Per-column filters
- Pagination
- Row selection (controlled/uncontrolled)
- Custom cell renderers
- Loading state
- Empty state

**Example:**
```tsx
interface User {
  id: number;
  name: string;
  email: string;
}

const columns: Column<User>[] = [
  { key: 'name', header: 'Name', sortable: true },
  { key: 'email', header: 'Email', sortable: true }
];

<DataTable<User> data={users} columns={columns} />
```

Use React hooks, no external table libraries.

performanceBenchmarks.name: process-small-dataset
performanceBenchmarks.code: const data = Array.from({length: 10}, (_, i) => ({id: i, name: "User" + i, age: 20 + i})); const columns = [{key: "name", header: "Name"}, {key: "age", header: "Age"}]; for (let i = 0; i < 1000; i++) { const filtered = data.filter(d => d.age > 20); }

performanceBenchmarks.name: process-large-dataset
performanceBenchmarks.code: const data = Array.from({length: 1000}, (_, i) => ({id: i, name: "User" + i, age: 20 + i})); const sorted = data.sort((a, b) => a.name.localeCompare(b.name)); const filtered = sorted.filter(d => d.age > 25);
